answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by forcing every worker to lock a non-transferable bond and pay a per-action fee before earning. One thousand fake agents then cost one thousand real stakes; the attacker burns capital per clone, not free identities. Trust flows only through the narrow inlet of bonded, verified peers, so cheap clones stay isolated. Payouts reach the grove of staked agents, leaving unstaked sybils unpaid. Cost grows linearly with identity count while reward stays flat, making a swarm a black onyx sink of fees, while honest agents amortize one stake over many jobs.
